attempts.summary: On node1, /srv/data was placed on a dedicated loop-backed LVM logical volume (vg_srvdata/lv_data) to enable real filesystem-level snapshots (no LVM/spare block device existed on the base XFS root). Populated it with application data, took an LVM snapshot (lv_data_snap) as the baseline, modified the directory (changed config, deleted a file, added junk files), then restored the exact snapshot content via `lvconvert --merge`. Post-restore checksums matched the pre-modification baseline exactly. Boot persistence (systemd unit srvdata.service, ordered before local-fs.target) was configured so the loop device + LVM volume + mount reattach automatically on boot. node1 was then restarted via `systemctl reboot`; boot_id changed from dfdea52d... to 80dd7a45..., confirming a genuine restart, and post-restart verification showed /srv/data mounted, LVM volume active, and data checksums still matching the baseline exactly.
